N62787.exp:

N62787.expe:

📌 पर: feel pity for someone; have mercy on someone।
✖ for — 'feel pity for' में आता है, 'take pity for' नहीं; with, at — इस idiom में प्रयोग नहीं।
N63168.expe:
✔ The idiom is 'take pity on someone': took pity on the beggar. Correct sentence: Naveen took pity on the beggar.
📌 But: feel pity for someone; have mercy on someone.
✖ for — used in 'feel pity for', not 'take pity for'; with, at — not used in this idiom.

N63169.exp:
✔ सही वाक्य: 'Hardly had Rekha left when Ramesh arrived.' — 'Hardly/Scarcely' के साथ 'when' और 'No sooner' के साथ 'than' आता है; वाक्य के आरंभ में ये आने पर inversion होता है (had + subject)।
📌 उदाहरण: Hardly had I reached when it rained। No sooner had I reached than it rained।
✖ B) No sooner, when — No sooner के साथ than आता है, when नहीं। C) Scarcely, than — Scarcely के साथ when आता है, than नहीं। D) Hardly, than — Hardly के साथ when आता है, than नहीं।
N63169.expe:
✔ Correct sentence: 'Hardly had Rekha left when Ramesh arrived.' — 'Hardly/Scarcely' pairs with 'when', and 'No sooner' pairs with 'than'; at the start of a sentence they take inversion (had + subject).
📌 Examples: Hardly had I reached when it rained. No sooner had I reached than it rained.
✖ B) No sooner, when — 'No sooner' takes 'than', not 'when'. C) Scarcely, than — 'Scarcely' takes 'when', not 'than'. D) Hardly, than — 'Hardly' takes 'when', not 'than'.

N63171.exp:
✔ 'fondness for' = किसी चीज़ का शौक — a fondness for sweets। सही वाक्य: Ravi has a fondness for sweets.
📌 पर adjective में: fond of sweets। समान: liking for, love for।
✖ of/to/in — 'fondness' के साथ ये prepositions मानक प्रयोग में नहीं आते; सही collocation 'fondness for' है।
N63171.expe:
✔ The noun 'fondness' takes 'for': a fondness for sweets. Correct sentence: Ravi has a fondness for sweets.
📌 But the adjective takes 'of': fond of sweets. Similar: liking for, love for.
✖ of/to/in — not idiomatic with 'fondness'; the correct collocation is 'fondness for'.

N63172.exp:
✔ सही वाक्य: 'Both Komal and Vijay are present.' — 'Both … and' — दो subjects जुड़कर plural बनते हैं, इसलिए verb 'are' के साथ 'Both A and B are present' सही।
📌 either…or / neither…nor में verb पास वाले subject के अनुसार; दोनों singular हों तो verb singular (is)।
✖ A) Either, or — दो singular subjects के साथ verb 'is' होती, 'are' नहीं। B) Both, as well as — both के साथ 'and' आता है, as well as नहीं। C) Neither, nor — दो singular subjects के साथ verb 'is' होती।
N63172.expe:
✔ Correct sentence: 'Both Komal and Vijay are present.' — 'Both ... and' joins two subjects into a plural, matching the verb 'are': Both A and B are present.
📌 With either...or / neither...nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject; two singular subjects take 'is'.
✖ A) Either, or — two singular subjects would need 'is', not 'are'. B) Both, as well as — 'both' pairs with 'and', not 'as well as'. C) Neither, nor — two singular subjects would need 'is'.

N63173.exp:
✔ 'Ravi entered the room.' — 'enter' के बाद preposition नहीं — 'entered the room' सही; यह वाक्य पूर्णतः सही है।
📌 'enter into' केवल समझौते के लिए: enter into an agreement।
✖ B) गलत — perfect tense में समय-बिंदु के साथ 'since' — 'has been ill since Monday'। C) गलत — 'good at' सही — 'good at English'। D) गलत — खेलों के नाम से पहले 'the' नहीं लगता — 'plays cricket' सही।
N63173.expe:
✔ 'Ravi entered the room.' — 'enter' takes a direct object — 'entered the room' is correct; this sentence is fully correct.
📌 'Enter into' is for agreements: enter into an agreement.
✖ B) wrong — with a perfect tense, a point of time takes 'since' — 'since Monday'. C) wrong — it should be 'good at' — 'good at English'. D) wrong — no article before names of games — 'plays cricket'.

📌 इसी तरह: acquainted with, familiar with।

N63174.expe:

📌 Similarly: acquainted with, familiar with.
✖ to/of/on — not idiomatic with 'conversant'; the correct collocation is 'conversant with'.

N63175.exp:

📌 उदाहरण: Hardly had I reached when it rained। No sooner had I reached than it rained।
✖ A) No sooner, when — No sooner के साथ than आता है, when नहीं। B) Hardly, than — Hardly के साथ when आता है, than नहीं। D) Scarcely, then — 'then' गलत; Scarcely … when होता है।
N63175.expe:

✖ A) No sooner, when — 'No sooner' takes 'than', not 'when'. B) Hardly, than — 'Hardly' takes 'when', not 'than'. D) Scarcely, then — 'then' is wrong; it is 'Scarcely ... when'.

N63176.exp:
✔ 'Rahul prefers tea to coffee.' — 'prefer … to' — 'prefers tea to coffee' सही; यह वाक्य पूर्णतः सही है।

✖ in/of/to — 'fondness' के साथ ये prepositions मानक प्रयोग में नहीं आते; सही collocation 'fondness for' है।

N63178.exp:
✔ सही वाक्य: 'The more Rahul earns, the more he spends.' — दो comparatives की समानांतर तुलना में 'The + comparative …, the + comparative …' संरचना आती है — The more he earns, the more he spends।
📌 अन्य उदाहरण: The sooner, the better। The higher you climb, the colder it gets।
✖ A) The, a — दूसरे भाग में भी 'the' चाहिए। C) A, the — comparative के साथ 'a' नहीं; दोनों जगह 'the'। D) More, the — 'More more' निरर्थक; पहले भाग में 'The' चाहिए।
N63178.expe:
✔ Correct sentence: 'The more Rahul earns, the more he spends.' — Parallel increase is shown by 'The + comparative ..., the + comparative ...': The more he earns, the more he spends.
📌 More examples: The sooner, the better. The higher you climb, the colder it gets.
✖ A) The, a — the second part also needs 'the'. C) A, the — 'a' cannot be used; both parts need 'the'. D) More, the — 'More more' is meaningless; the first part needs 'The'.

N63179.exp:
✔ 'He discussed the problem.' — 'discuss' के बाद सीधे object — 'discussed the problem' सही; यह वाक्य पूर्णतः सही है।
📌 पर noun: a discussion about the problem।
✖ A) गलत — 'married to' सही है, 'married with' नहीं। B) गलत — honest का h silent — 'an honest officer'। D) गलत — 'Hardly' के साथ 'when' — 'Hardly had … when …'।
N63179.expe:
✔ 'He discussed the problem.' — 'discuss' takes a direct object — 'discussed the problem' is correct; this sentence is fully correct.
📌 But the noun: a discussion about the problem.
✖ A) wrong — it should be 'married to', not 'married with'. B) wrong — the 'h' in 'honest' is silent — 'an honest officer'. D) wrong — 'Hardly' pairs with 'when' — 'Hardly had ... when ...'.

📌 अन्य उदाहरण: The sooner, the better। The higher you climb, the colder it gets।
✖ B) More, the — 'More more' निरर्थक; पहले भाग में 'The' चाहिए। C) A, the — comparative के साथ 'a' नहीं; दोनों जगह 'the'। D) The, a — दूसरे भाग में भी 'the' चाहिए।

N63182.exp:
✔ 'Though Priya is poor, yet she is honest.' — 'Though … yet …' सही correlative है; यह वाक्य पूर्णतः सही है।
📌 though/although के साथ but नहीं आता।
✖ A) गलत — 'enter' (प्रवेश करना) के बाद into नहीं — 'entered the room'। C) गलत — 'neither' के साथ 'nor' आता है — 'Neither … nor …'। D) गलत — दो के लिए 'between' — 'divided the money between the two sons'।
N63182.expe:
✔ 'Though Priya is poor, yet she is honest.' — 'Though ... yet ...' is a correct correlative; this sentence is fully correct.
📌 'Though/although' never pairs with 'but'.
✖ A) wrong — 'enter' (go into a place) takes no preposition — 'entered the room'. C) wrong — 'neither' pairs with 'nor' — 'Neither ... nor ...'. D) wrong — for two, use 'between' — 'between the two sons'.

N63183.exp:
✔ 'cure somebody of (a disease)' — cured of fever (बुखार से ठीक हुआ)। सही वाक्य: The boy was cured of fever.
📌 पर noun: a cure for fever (बुखार का इलाज)। समान: rid of, relieved of।
✖ by — इलाज करने वाले (कर्ता) के लिए (cured by the doctor), रोग के लिए नहीं; to, with — मानक नहीं।
N63183.expe:
✔ 'Cure someone of a disease': cured of fever. Correct sentence: The boy was cured of fever.
📌 But the noun takes 'for': a cure for fever. Similar: rid of, relieved of.
✖ by — names the agent (cured by the doctor), not the disease; to, with — not idiomatic.

N63184.exp:
✔ सही वाक्य: 'Neither Radha nor Usha was present.' — 'Neither … nor' (न … न) — Neither A nor B was present। दो singular subjects होने पर verb singular (was) रहता है।
📌 neither…nor / either…or में verb पास वाले subject के अनुसार (proximity rule)।
✖ A) Neither, or — neither के साथ nor आता है, or नहीं। B) Either, nor — either के साथ or आता है, nor नहीं। C) Both, nor — both के साथ and आता है और verb plural (were) होगी।
N63184.expe:
✔ Correct sentence: 'Neither Radha nor Usha was present.' — 'Neither ... nor' (not one and not the other): Neither A nor B was present; with two singular subjects the verb is singular.
📌 With neither...nor / either...or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (proximity rule).
✖ A) Neither, or — 'neither' pairs with 'nor', not 'or'. B) Either, nor — 'either' pairs with 'or', not 'nor'. C) Both, nor — 'both' pairs with 'and' and takes a plural verb.

N63185.exp:
✔ 'He is afraid from snakes.' गलत है — 'afraid of' सही — 'afraid of snakes'।
📌 इसी तरह: scared of, frightened of।
✖ B) सही — खेल के नाम से पहले article नहीं लगता — 'plays cricket' सही। C) सही — 'enter' के बाद preposition नहीं — 'entered the room' सही। D) सही — 'unless' = if not; इसके साथ दूसरा negative नहीं — वाक्य सही।
N63185.expe:
✔ 'He is afraid from snakes.' is incorrect — it should be 'afraid of' — 'afraid of snakes'.
📌 Similarly: scared of, frightened of.
✖ B) correct — no article before a game — 'plays cricket' is correct. C) correct — 'enter' takes a direct object — 'entered the room' is correct. D) correct — 'unless' = 'if not'; no extra negative — correct.

N63186.exp:
✔ 'vulnerable to' = किसी चीज़ के प्रति असुरक्षित/ग्रहणशील — vulnerable to infection। सही वाक्य: Sunita is vulnerable to infection.
📌 इसी तरह: prone to, susceptible to, liable to।
✖ for/from/with — 'vulnerable' के साथ ये prepositions मानक प्रयोग में नहीं आते; सही collocation 'vulnerable to' है।
N63186.expe:
✔ 'Vulnerable to' means open to harm from: vulnerable to infection. Correct sentence: Sunita is vulnerable to infection.
📌 Similarly: prone to, susceptible to, liable to.
✖ for/from/with — not idiomatic with 'vulnerable'; the correct collocation is 'vulnerable to'.

N63187.exp:
✔ सही वाक्य: 'Jyoti is not only honest but also intelligent.' — 'not only … but also' correlative conjunction की निश्चित जोड़ी है — He is not only honest but also intelligent।
📌 अन्य correlatives: either…or, neither…nor, both…and, whether…or।
✖ A) both, as well as — both के साथ 'and' आता है। B) either, nor — either के साथ 'or' आता है। D) not only, as well as — not only के साथ 'but also' आता है, as well as नहीं।
N63187.expe:
✔ Correct sentence: 'Jyoti is not only honest but also intelligent.' — 'Not only ... but also' is a fixed correlative pair: He is not only honest but also intelligent.
📌 Other correlatives: either...or, neither...nor, both...and, whether...or.
✖ A) both, as well as — 'both' pairs with 'and'. B) either, nor — 'either' pairs with 'or'. D) not only, as well as — 'not only' takes 'but also', not 'as well as'.

N63188.exp:
✔ 'Usha has been ill from Monday.' गलत है — perfect tense में समय-बिंदु के साथ 'since' — 'has been ill since Monday'।
📌 'from' के साथ आमतौर पर अंत-बिंदु: from Monday to Friday।
✖ A) सही — h silent, vowel sound — 'an honest officer' सही। B) सही — दो के बीच बाँटने के लिए 'between' सही। C) सही — अवधि के साथ 'for' — 'for five years' सही।
N63188.expe:
✔ 'Usha has been ill from Monday.' is incorrect — with a perfect tense, a point of time takes 'since' — 'since Monday'.
📌 'From' usually pairs with an end point: from Monday to Friday.
✖ A) correct — silent 'h', vowel sound — 'an honest officer' is correct. B) correct — 'between' is correct for two. C) correct — a period takes 'for' — 'for five years' is correct.

N63190.exp:

📌 रूपांतरण: so weak that he cannot stand = too weak to stand। 'such' के बाद noun आता है: such a weak man that…।

N63190.expe:
✔ Correct sentence: 'Rohan is so weak that he cannot stand.' — 'so + adjective + that + clause': He is so weak that he cannot stand.
📌 Transformation: so weak that he cannot stand = too weak to stand. 'Such' is followed by a noun: such a weak man that...
✖ A) too, that — 'too' takes 'to + verb', not a that-clause. C) so, as — 'so ... as' is for comparison (not so tall as). D) such, that — 'such' needs a noun, not a bare adjective.

✖ A) गलत — 'unless' स्वयं नकारात्मक (if not) है, इसलिए 'does not' नहीं — 'Unless he works hard'। B) गलत — 'No sooner' के साथ 'than' — 'No sooner had … than …'। D) गलत — 'good at' सही — 'good at English'।
N63191.expe:

N63193.exp:
✔ सही वाक्य: 'Vikas is too weak to stand.' — 'too + adjective + to + verb' = इतना … कि … नहीं — He is too weak to stand (इतना कमज़ोर कि खड़ा नहीं हो सकता)। too में ही नकारात्मक अर्थ है।

N63194.exp:
